claims.exact_statement: For fixed spin S and fixed positive spatial nearest-neighbor couplings J_1,J_2,J_3, the zero-field finite-volume Gibbs state of H=-sum_x sum_i J_i S_x dot S_{x+e_i} on even periodic cubic tori should, at every sufficiently low fixed positive beta, satisfy the spherical magnetization transform limit sinh(m|t|)/(m|t|), where m is the right derivative at zero of the thermodynamic pressure in a field along axis 3, and normalized total-spin squared tends to m^2.
assumptions: S is a fixed positive half-integer.
J_i are fixed positive constants, bounded away from zero; bonds are ferromagnetic and retain full SU(2) spin symmetry.
The limit is through even periodic cubes; beta is fixed after choosing a sufficiently low-temperature threshold depending on S and J.
The measured quantities are self-adjoint linear combinations of spin components; no joint finite-volume vector measurement is assumed.
claims.status: conditional internal proof-transfer candidate; weighted Nash/flow and pressure-Laplacian substitutions are reconstructed, but all conditioned-cycle and sparse-pin estimates have not been independently audited end to end; theorem and priority UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: The pinned spherical-law manuscript states the isotropic nearest-neighbor result; its separate Bloch-law companion allows anisotropic finite-range couplings but does not state this spherical distribution. Targeted web search found no direct independent anisotropic spherical-law source; priority remains UNKNOWN and the OpenAI source has no independent build/expert review recorded.
claims.costs: Mathematical oracle: exact finite-volume Gibbs expectations; the proof gives an asymptotic law but no finite-size bias rate. A proposed material test needs R equilibrium specimen/readout runs or R*V local spin readouts, plus material-specific J_i calibration; finite specimen size, equilibration time, instrument precision, and financial costs remain UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: A broken weighted conditional next-pin identity or sparse-pin estimate under direction-dependent rates, failure of the weighted Laplacian positivity/cancellation, or a verified counterexample with all J_i>0 and SU(2)-invariant scalar bonds falsifies this transfer.
claims.next_gate: Audit Sections 2-5 of the source line by line with rates J_i/2, propagate J_min/J_max constants through every sparse-pin induction step, adapt the variational pressure endpoint, then seek independent expert proof review and a complete priority search.

claims.exact_statement: The valid absorbing CTMCs A=(alpha=(1,0), T=[[-3,1],[0,-1]], r=(2,1)^T) and B=(alpha=(1,0), T=[[-11/4,3/4],[7/12,-5/4]], r=(2,2/3)^T) have the same full activation-time density (3/2)e^(-3t)+(1/2)e^(-t) and the same activation-before-independent-Exp(delta)-off probability for every delta>=0, despite A being one-way sequential and B containing a positive reverse transition.
assumptions: Known initial transient state 1; two hidden transient states and one absorbing activation event.
Only activation-time records or activation-before-independent-exponential-off outputs are observed; no intermediate state is measured.
Rates are fixed, time homogeneous, and nonnegative.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact construction and symbolically checked; general similarity nonidentifiability is established phase-type prior art; no TCR biological finding or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Phase-type representation similarity is classical prior art. Morita-Groves 2025 already articulate sequential-vs-parallel ITAM/LAT models. The matrix pair is an exact scoped witness and is not asserted to match a real receptor or the multithread model.
claims.costs: Activation/FPT data cannot identify A versus B even with infinitely many exact samples; equal-prior minimax error is 1/2. An ideal known-rate binary state-2 occupancy read at t=(log 3)/2 gives gap 1/(12 sqrt(3)); 2,589 independent episodes suffice for one-sided 0.05 Hoeffding error. Reporter calibration, biological clustering, track loss, physical episode count, and money are UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the exact similarity identities, transient-generator row sums/rate validity, equal Laplace transforms, or occupancy-gap calculation falsifies the displayed witness. A state-specific observation outside predictions rejects this pair only.
claims.next_gate: Pilot same-receptor per-ITAM/ZAP70 intermediate-state and LAT-condensation tracking under controlled randomized ligand dwell times, then evaluate parameter-matched sequential/multithread models on held-out dwell times and ITAM perturbations.

claims.exact_statement: For the periodic low-temperature 2D square-lattice Ising model at dimensionless fields s=+-c/N, Borgs-Kotecky finite-size scaling yields one-site means +-m_* tanh(m_*c)+o(1); therefore an oracle supplying only the shared interval [-c/N,c/N] cannot guarantee vanishing one-site TV error.
assumptions: Periodic square torus with N=L^2 spins and fixed low-temperature K in the contour regime.
Dimensionless uniform field s lies in [-c/N,c/N] but its exact value is not supplied.
The target is a one-site Gibbs marginal; equilibrium sampling availability is not assumed.
claims.status: scout-derived exact consequence of established finite-size scaling; no new theorem or priority claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Borgs-Kotecky first-order finite-size scaling preempts the coexistence counterexample mechanism; the new framing is only an application-specific calibration lower bound.
claims.costs: An ideal local readout needs O(a_c^-2 log(1/delta)) equilibrium samples; phase switching/equilibration may be exponentially costly and remains uncharged/UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch in field normalization or failure of the low-temperature contour assumptions invalidates the finite-size scaling input.
claims.next_gate: Seek a local-observable Gibbs-TV theorem conditional on an acquired integrated susceptibility/correlation-sum bound, and test it on a named calibrated material.
